tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description uses imperative phrasing ('Use this skill when a user asks to...', 'Activate on requests like...', 'Also activate when...'), focuses on user intent (reviewing/auditing sustainability posture, carbon footprint, emissions) rather than internal implementation, and explicitly enumerates many trigger contexts (specific phrases, CSV attachments, AI/ML workload mentions, Graviton questions). It is slightly long but remains within a reasonable paragraph length given the breadth of triggers it needs to cover for correct activation.
tests.evidence: Use this skill when a user asks to review or audit a workload's sustainability posture, carbon footprint, emissions, water usage, environmental impact, or resource efficiency. Activate on requests like "sustainability review", "carbon footprint analysis"...

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body avoids explaining general concepts (e.g., what carbon emissions are, what HTTP calls do) and instead focuses on domain-specific conventions, exact API call parameters, attribution ordering, and non-obvious caveats (reporting thresholds, lag windows, severity definitions). It is dense but every line conveys project-specific knowledge.
tests.evidence: 'Absent or zero emissions are below the reporting threshold (0.5 g CO2e, 0.5 mL water), not zero impact. Carbon for month M publishes by the 21st of M+1...' — this is non-obvious domain knowledge, not general explanation.

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: The body keeps detailed reference material (API parameter lists, metric formulas, 29-practice checklist, thresholds) out of the body and defers to references/ files loaded conditionally at each step; the body only gives short pointers and summarized rules.
tests.evidence: 'Load [references/sus-best-practices-checklist.md](references/sus-best-practices-checklist.md). For every practice, apply its evidence, NOT MET / PARTIAL criteria...' — detail is deferred to the reference file, not embedded.

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: Every file in references/ is linked with a markdown link in the body (workload-model.md, proxy-metrics.md, framing-and-attribution.md, emissions-collection.md, emissions-api-reference.md, ai-ml-workloads.md, graviton-migration.md, csv-emissions-input.md, sus-best-practices-checklist.md).
tests.evidence: '[references/workload-model.md](references/workload-model.md)', '[references/csv-emissions-input.md](references/csv-emissions-input.md)' — all nine reference files have corresponding markdown links.

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: Each reference link is tied to a specific step and condition, e.g. loading ai-ml-workloads.md only when ML shape detected, or csv-emissions-input.md when a CSV is attached, clearly specifying when to load.
tests.evidence: 'ML / accelerated shape, or `Invocations` in the `AWS/Bedrock` namespace → load [references/ai-ml-workloads.md](references/ai-ml-workloads.md).'

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All reference links use relative paths rooted at references/ with no absolute paths or traversal.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile, high-risk operations (API call parameters, attribution order, severity rules, read-only constraint) are prescribed exactly, while flexible parts (scope selection, business metric fallback, topology walk) allow agent judgment with rationale given.
tests.evidence: 'Never call `Modify*`, `Delete*`, `Terminate*` or `Create*`. Every recommendation is for a human to action.' paired with 'Ask for the scope... If there is none, use the first available fallback and state its caveat' — prescriptive where fragile, flexible where variable.

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: Where multiple options exist (e.g., business output metric fallbacks, failure handling), a clear priority order/default is given rather than presenting equal choices.
tests.evidence: '1. Request count ... 2. Invocation count ... 3. Data processed ... 4. None — report absolute footprint only' — ordered fallback list, not an undifferentiated menu.

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The workflow teaches a generalizable 9-step procedure (scope, topology, shape detection, KPI derivation, assessment, reporting) applicable to any workload, not a one-off declaration for a specific account or resource.
tests.evidence: 'Step 2 — Topology ... Walk the Agent Space topology from the entry point, classify every resource into a layer, and record each resource's Region.' — generalizes across any workload.

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: The 'Critical — read first' section functions as an extensive gotchas list with concrete, non-obvious corrections (reporting thresholds, lag timing, attribution order, AccessDeniedException handling, month-length comparison).
tests.evidence: 'Compare months per day. A 28-day month carries about 10% less than a 31-day one at the same usage; a delta smaller than the day-count difference is not a finding.'

tests.name: Templates and outputs missing
tests.reasoning: The skill produces a report and explicitly provides a template asset referenced at Step 9, satisfying the need for structured output.
tests.evidence: 'Load [assets/report-template.md](assets/report-template.md). Create one report artifact per workload...'

tests.name: Templates and outputs must not be in body
tests.reasoning: No large output template is embedded inline in the body; the report template is fully offloaded to assets/report-template.md and only referenced.
tests.evidence: 'Load [assets/report-template.md](assets/report-template.md) at Step 9 even when the user asks specific questions' — template content lives in assets, not body.

tests.name: Asset files must be linked
tests.reasoning: The single asset file report-template.md is linked multiple times in the body.
tests.evidence: 'Load [assets/report-template.md](assets/report-template.md).' appears in Step 9 and the critical section.

tests.name: Asset links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: The asset reference clearly specifies when to load it: at Step 9, for creating the report artifact.
tests.evidence: 'Load [assets/report-template.md](assets/report-template.md). Create one report artifact per workload, named `sustainability-review-<workload-name>-<YYYY-MM-DD>.md`...'

tests.name: Asset path format
tests.reasoning: The asset reference uses a relative path from skill root with no absolute path or traversal.

tests.name: Step-by-step guidance
tests.reasoning: The workflow is presented as an ordered checkbox checklist with Step N labels, and the detailed sections below use matching '### Step N — ...' headings referencing the same step numbers.
tests.evidence: '- [ ] Step 1: Scope and business output metric' ... '### Step 1 — Scope and business output metric' — checklist and detail sections align on step numbering.

tests.name: Validation loops
tests.reasoning: The skill includes an explicit pre-presentation validation checklist instructing the agent to verify its own report output for completeness and correctness before presenting it.
tests.evidence: 'Before presenting the report, check the draft and fix any failure: - [ ] All 29 practices have a status, and every MET cites evidence. - [ ] Every KPI and delta matches the collected data...'
